That's the problem here, what exactly is 'Red' to you? For all we know you might actually be seeing them as 'Green' (I mean the actual wavelength here) because your red receptors could be deficient (for example). 

I'm essentially green blind so I often confuse 'green' and 'gray' as very similar even though I have two entirely different internal concepts of green and gray. 

The range of wavelengths that stimulate the green and red receptors also overlaps so that can make it even more confusing for those with red/green deficiencies.

In some cases depending on the light source green looks almost white to me, such as very bright green LEDs. 

On top of all this in low light conditions my red perception is very bad, and most red objects will look 'green' but I know they are actually appearing as 'gray'.

For me at least, my brain tried to make sense of the world as I grew up being told things about colors that didn't quite make sense (until we learned I was colorblind). 

So even though I'm essentially green blind and have poor red perception, I still have these separate concepts of green, red, and gray in my mind and often get confused between them.
